items.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese arrived in Shenzhen on Tuesday afternoon ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders summit, where he says dialogue between nations is a 'good thing' even as Australia reaffirms its opposition to Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Albanese indicated he would likely appear in the traditional APEC family photo alongside Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, describing it as a matter of 'respect' for China as host and noting that if invited to an event he respects that while still making his position clear on Ukraine. He declined to follow former Prime Minister Tony Abbott's confrontational approach, saying he would not take lessons in diplomacy from the former prime minister who said he would 'shirt front' Putin at a 2014 G20 summit. Albanese characterised Moscow as 'a big power intervening in an illegal way,' framing Russia's actions against Ukraine as an attempt to assert its will while underestimating the Ukrainian people's conviction to fight for their national sovereignty, and insisted Australia's position remains unchanged. The annual gathering of 21 economies is expected to be overshadowed by a trilateral summit on Thursday between Putin, US President Donald Trump, and Chinese President Xi Jinping; Albanese said it was 'not up to Australia to determine who people have met with,' but reiterated that any solution or peace in Ukraine must be on 'Ukraine's terms.' Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned against the three leaders deciding his country's future without Kyiv at the table, likening the meeting to a modern-day Yalta conference. Albanese said he is due to sit down with Xi Jinping on Friday morning but would not foreshadow the issues he planned to raise. On domestic commitments, Albanese confirmed Labor's election promise to return the Port of Darwin lease into Australian hands before the 2028 election remains unchanged though he could not guarantee a timeline, noting there might be 'legal consequences and actions.' The port is leased to Chinese-owned company Landbridge in what has become a sensitive issue in the bilateral relationship. He also signalled continued pressure on China to remove barriers to Australian agricultural exports after tariffs exceeded an annual quota on beef, stating Australia would 'rather not have any quotas on Australian goods anywhere in the world,' while noting strong demand for Australian beef demonstrates appeal to Chinese consumers following a visit to a Shenzhen supermarket stocking local products including apples, cherries, beef and lobster. Albanese said trade with China is important for Australian jobs and economic growth.
items.title: Albanese arrives in Shenzhen ahead of APEC summit and Putin talks

items.summary: The leaders of China, the United States and Russia are due to hold their first-ever trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit this week. Separately, US President Donald Trump will also meet Chinese President Xi Jinping during the November 18-19 gathering in Shenzhen, China. Several experts interviewed by DW do not expect breakthroughs on US-China trade, technology or other issues; maintaining the existing trade truce and preventing bilateral relations from deteriorating further may be the more realistic shared objectives. Patricia M. Kim, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, believes neither leader is looking to significantly expand the bilateral agenda, as both have an incentive in maintaining the existing trade truce. Over the next two years, Kim expects "neither uncontrolled escalation in tensions between the US and China nor a dramatic improvement in ties, but rather the continuation of the transactional détente we see today." Zhang Lun, a professor at CY Cergy Paris University, believes Trump is under pressure both at home and abroad: domestically he faces becoming a lame-duck president following the Republicans' heavy losses in the midterm elections, while internationally damage to relations with allies, weakening of the US-led international order, indifference toward democratic values and freedoms, and difficulties encountered in the Iran war have all reduced America's leverage. Zhang believes these factors have weakened Trump's hand with Beijing, making him more eager to secure diplomatic wins and Xi's cooperation on key policy priorities. Jia Hui Tee, a senior trade policy analyst at the Hinrich Foundation, expects Trump and Xi to focus on stabilizing their fragile trade relationship. She says the two leaders could make progress on reciprocal tariff cuts covering goods worth $30 billion (€27.3 billion) on each side; while the list of products has been announced, the timeline has not been set and an indicative implementation timeline would be an easy win for both governments. Washington wants Beijing to accelerate purchases of US agricultural products and increase exports of rare earths and other critical minerals, but Tee believes China would likely be cautious with delivering on its commitments especially when Trump is weaker at home after the midterms with Democrats pushing back on his tariffs. She also points out that neither side would want to cede their bargaining chips easily, including rare earth exports and technology export controls. With another meeting between the two leaders expected in December at the G20 summit in Miami, there is room to push more contentious issues to a later date and further extend the trade truce in the next meeting. Regarding Russia's agenda, Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center, told DW that Moscow wants to create the impression that Washington is willing to sit down with Russia and negotiate, which could undermine confidence in Europe and Ukraine. "Trump wants trilateral nuclear talks," she said, while Beijing "wants the optics of China hosting the unprecedented historical meeting among the three." Alicja Bachulska, a policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, believes Beijing wants to use the meeting to demonstrate its ability to bring major powers together and facilitate international dialogue. She summarized each leader's aim as: "Russia wants recognition, the US wants arms control, and China wants status without strings attached," expecting each leader to restate their own positions rather than produce real solutions. On Ukraine mediation, Michael Kimmage, director of the Kennan Institute in the United States, told DW last month that China may be more concerned with the survival of Russian President Vladimir Putin's regime than with actively bringing the war in Ukraine to an end; Russia remains an important source of energy and a key diplomatic partner for Beijing. An outright Russian victory may not necessarily be Beijing's objective: "More important to China is the political survival of Vladimir Putin." For that reason, Kimmage does not expect China to pressure the Russian president into ending the war if Putin is unwilling to do so. Zhang Lun believes the current situation is "most in line with Beijing's interests," arguing that the Trump administration's pro-Putin stance has made it harder for Ukraine to resist Russia while Europe has been forced to bear greater costs and weakened, and that the United States has also lost moral authority as alliances built around Washington have eroded. He believes Beijing wants to keep Russia from collapsing but not support it so openly or extensively that it alienates Europe and other Western countries; at the same time China does not want Ukraine to be defeated because that would reduce Russia's dependence on Beijing. For now, China is unlikely to intervene directly, instead waiting for a more favorable moment and then potentially stepping in as a neutral mediator to maximize its gains. On Iran, W.A. Figueroa, an assistant professor of history and international relations at the University of Groningen in the Netherlands, told DW that there is little indication of any real cooperation between China and the US on Iran. The two countries do share some interests, "including opposition to a toll system in the Strait of Hormuz and opposition to nuclear proliferation," but "China has consistently called for negotiations and denounced both sanctions and military force as a way to achieve these or any other objectives." Figueroa says China does not want further escalation or prolonged instability in the Middle East. However, Beijing has been able to manage the current situation without too much difficulty, leaving it with little pressure to change its position; "China continues to provide Iran with crucial financial support through its purchases of Iranian oil," and Beijing's diplomatic support has so far brought no substantial change largely because China has little leverage over either Iran or the US in the region. No visual was selected because the document offers only qualitative expert assessments rather than comparable numeric relationships suitable for charting; figures such as $30 billion (€27.3 billion) are embedded within narrative claims about tariff cuts and cannot stand alone as a plotted comparison, so prose is the appropriate form.
items.title: Expert expectations for Trump–Xi and US–China–Russia trilateral talks at APEC Shenzhen summit

In the Iran war, Iran's army said it launched drones at US installations at Kuwait's Ali Al Salem Air Base, with Kuwait engaging but not confirming a hit; Bahrain intercepted several Iranian attacks early Wednesday after Iran's Revolutionary Guard targeted a radar system there on Monday. Britain imposed sanctions under Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband targeting eight construction and property firms involved in illegal settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank and a group blocking aid to Gaza; this was the first package since September's reset of the UK's approach, intended to disrupt their finance flows. Separately, US immigration authorities detained former world boxing champion Jorge Linares at El Paso International Airport after he overstayed his authorized stay; ICE spokeswoman Leticia Zamarripa said he entered on Oct. 26, 2023 with temporary permission and is held at the El Paso Processing Center, though lawyers say he is in the country legally. A Spanish court sentenced a Real Oviedo supporter to 11 months for racially abusing Kylian Mbappe during an August 2025 La Liga match, fining him and suspending the sentence on condition he stay away from stadiums hosting official events for two years; Real Madrid took part as private prosecutor. items.summary: In an interview with Anadolu Agency on the sidelines of COP31's second week in Antalya, Türkiye, on 18 November 2026, Zaghloul Samhan, head of the Palestinian Environment Quality Authority, called for the summit to explicitly recognize countries under occupation and crisis as highly vulnerable. He argued that developed nations should pay for their climate effects while developing countries benefit from the resulting finance, urging delegates to prioritize adaptation over emissions cuts given developing states' minimal share of global emissions and disproportionate exposure to climate impacts. Samhan stressed Palestine's core priority is giving such countries precedence in assessing resource needs and financing, easing access to financial resources as well as environmental and climate funds. He specifically requested that Palestine gain access to the Global Environment Facility (GEF) project funds one day, while procedures for accessing the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and other environmental funds be streamlined; both mechanisms serve as main financial arms of the UN climate framework but political restrictions have barred Palestine from major GEF project funds, and GCF financing has remained limited due to lengthy accreditation and project-approval hurdles. Unlocking these funds would allow Palestine to carry out adaptation and mitigation projects outlined in its nationally determined contributions (NDCs). Samhan also underscored the urgent need for resources to rebuild Gaza's devastated environmental infrastructure, noting that around 97% of the enclave's agricultural land is either contaminated or inaccessible to Palestinians; a joint UN Food and Agriculture Organization and UNOSAT satellite assessment confirmed only 3% of Gaza's cropland remained accessible and undamaged as of August 2026, while a World Bank–UN–EU report estimates agriculture and food-system reconstruction needs at nearly $10.5 billion. He said the scale of destruction requires sweeping reconstruction across virtually every environmental sector—destroyed wastewater networks and treatment plants, renewable energy facilities, solid waste systems, medical and hazardous waste facilities, plus water infrastructure such as groundwater wells, desalination plants, distribution networks and reservoirs—and flagged Wadi Gaza's nature reserve as one of the most polluted areas in Gaza. Damaged sewage and waste systems have left raw wastewater and debris flowing into the Mediterranean, contaminating coastal and marine ecosystems; Samhan warned enormous financial backing will be needed to restore basic services, farmland and natural environment. Despite obstacles, he expressed optimism about progress at the summit, citing Türkiye's COP31 presidency as a source of support and praising its hosting as one of the best COPs he ever attended.
items.title: Palestinian environment chief calls for COP31 climate finance access and Gaza reconstruction funding

items.summary: On Thursday, Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, and Donald Trump are meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China. The article frames this gathering as a rare chance for the leaders of the world's three major powers to exchange views directly on global issues, drawing comparisons to the 1945 Yalta conference when Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin divided the world into spheres of influence after World War II. However, it argues that Shenzhen is not 'Yalta 2.0' nor an isolated episode: in May this year Xi hosted back-to-back visits by Trump and Putin to Beijing; Trump reciprocated by hosting Xi in Washington in September and meeting with Putin in Alaska last year. Taken together, these developments signal a broader shift away from the post-Cold War emphasis on global institutions and multilateral consultations toward a more personalised form of great-power management that is likely 'the new normal': a world in which China, Russia, and the US act as an informal steering committee for global affairs, with Europe and other middle powers increasingly on the sidelines. The article notes these three remain strategic competitors but share an understanding of conducting international politics through direct engagement among few major powers rather than institutions or coalitions; this is described not as a formal alliance—even between China and Russia—or a coordinated redesign of the international system, but as a common instinct toward great-power management in which major powers enjoy special rights and privileged voices while limiting others' involvement. As evidence, it cites that Russia and the US just concluded a third round of peace talks this year in Abu Dhabi towards ending the Ukraine war, during which Ukraine was part of discussions but European negotiators were not; Trump has flagged as possible a new security framework for Europe modelled after Cold War spheres of influence, saying the US is working on a big deal to end the war that would include 'all of Europe'; and Jared Kushner said Washington wanted Europe in the process while adding finding someone who could credibly speak for Europe might be harder than persuading Russia to include them. Xi's agreement to join the Shenzhen trilateral summit risks legitimising Europe's exclusion, even though Ukraine is not on the agenda; this looks awkward for China given Xi's repeated emphasis on multipolarity and criticism of Cold War-style politics dominated by a few major powers, and Beijing's previous stress that Europe should be 'at the table' for Ukraine discussions. The article observes that despite these tensions, China's Foreign Ministry described the summit as having 'groundbreaking significance,' with the three leaders to 'exchange views in depth on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations,' suggesting Beijing accepts a diplomacy model centred on major powers to the exclusion of others—an uncomfortable reality for Europe, which remains one of the world's largest economic and technological centres but struggles to translate that weight into a unified strategic voice. Turning to middle powers, the article argues their return to relevance does not mean they are irrelevant: European nations, Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea, and key Southeast Asian nations may lack the military capabilities or geopolitical heft to alter the distribution of power in the international system, but they retain institutions, networks, and coalitions that can help shape rules, sustain institutions, and build partnerships capable of constraining larger states. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's call for closer middle-power cooperation reflects this logic—rather than choosing sides in great-power rivalry, he has recognised the necessity to 'stop pretending, to name the reality' while 'building coalitions that work – issue by issue, with partners who share enough common ground to act together.' The article concludes that as global power concentrates in fewer leaders' hands, middle powers have stronger incentives to cooperate; they are unlikely to decide the overall direction of world order but can still influence the rules, norms, and institutions through which it operates. The central question raised by Shenzhen is therefore not whether a handful of major powers will continue exercising disproportionate influence—they will—but how the rest of the world will respond.
items.title: Xi-Trump-Putin Shenzhen Summit and the Rise of Great-Power Management

items.summary: On Wednesday, Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said on the chipmaker's earnings call for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 that the company has no plan to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive. This came hours after Huang posted his first public statement since resigning, saying he would be honoured to return if the board decided it was in the best interest of the company while admitting serious mistakes in his personal life and committing to cooperate with the board's independent investigation. Jones stated that Huang had voluntarily resigned his positions as President, CEO, and Board member after disclosure of personal behaviour inconsistent with Nvidia's code of conduct standards and cultural norms, adding that the board unanimously accepted the resignation and does not intend to reinstate him as CEO. The November 12 statement announcing the resignation had not given a reason at the time. Jones said the board has retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to lead the search for a permanent chief executive, with CFO Colette Kress serving as interim CEO; he expressed that the board has every confidence in Kress's leadership and ability to deliver. The board also established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee comprising independent directors, senior external advisers, and legal counsel to enhance engagement with US government agencies. Huang's exit followed media reports alleging an extramarital relationship with a Chinese businesswoman reportedly suspected by US authorities of spying for Beijing; the board opened an independent investigation after reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, and President Donald Trump said on November 8 that the FBI was also investigating. More than 1.98 lakh people, including over 10,024 who say they are current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter seeking Huang's reinstatement as of early Wednesday according to standwithjensen.com, with Tesla CEO Elon Musk among signatories; since his departure, employees, investors, business partners, and customers have called for his return. On the financial side, Nvidia's net income more than doubled to USD 65.3 billion for the quarter ended October 25, 2026 from USD 31.9 billion a year earlier; revenue rose 103 per cent to USD 115.8 billion from USD 57 billion in the year-ago quarter and was up 20 per cent sequentially, with data centre business revenue rising 110 per cent year-on-year to USD 107.6 billion. Kress said Nvidia's momentum is real and that it remains an exceptional technology leader; for the fourth quarter, which includes an additional week, Nvidia expects revenue of USD 130 billion plus or minus 3 per cent. The article was published on November 18, 2026.
items.title: Nvidia board declines to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO despite his offer; Q3 fiscal 2027 results reported strong

items.summary: Shares of HFCL and Sterlite Tech each rallied about 5% after Nvidia reported strong earnings, marking a rebound following more than 10% declines over two prior days. The gains occurred despite concerns that the Democratic Party's victory in US midterm elections could tighten restrictions on data centre expansion and slow AI infrastructure development. Nvidia's results are viewed as positive for HFCL and Sterlite Tech because they reinforce expectations of sustained global AI-infrastructure spending, which depends on extensive optical fibre networks for high-speed, low-latency connectivity between servers and facilities. The company also navigated leadership transition questions following the departure of longtime CEO Jensen Huang; it declined to entertain inquiries about his resignation and had no plans to reinstate him. Interim CEO Colette Kress told investors that Nvidia expects revenue to grow 75% in fiscal 2028. Separately, Michael O'Rourke at JonesTrading warned that a data centre slowdown from the political shift would be real, arguing that earnings estimates underpinning bullish valuations are no longer valid and that investors lack clarity on where those estimates will reset, prompting de-risking until conditions improve. Jakub Rochlitz at eToro noted this differs from typical sell-offs because recoveries did not follow significant losses such as Intel Corp.'s plunge of almost 30% on Friday; he also pointed to rising cross-sector correlation and volatility spreading the rout across markets. Chris Zaccarelli at Northlight Asset Management described the all-or-nothing mentality as surprising, agreeing that sentiment has shifted and data centre construction will become more difficult, but asserting that facilities with a productive business case will still be built. The next major indicator of investor appetite for the AI sector is expected from Anthropic's share pricing later Wednesday ahead of its market debut, which could value the company at up to $1.4 trillion as it targets an IPO price near or above the upper end of its range, per Bloomberg News.
items.title: HFCL and Sterlite Tech shares rally on Nvidia's strong earnings amid AI-infrastructure concerns

items.summary:
In today's session, Indian IT stocks fell after Nvidia reported strong earnings that eased broader concerns about the artificial intelligence sector. TCS shares dipped 2.5% to Rs 2,382, while Infosys was down almost a per cent to Rs 1,113. Wipro also slipped over a per cent, and HCL Tech and Tech Mahindra fell up to 1%. Nvidia's results came amid continued investor assessment of the company's leadership transition following longtime CEO Jensen Huang's departure; Nvidia said it would not entertain questions about his resignation and had no plans to reinstate him. Interim CEO Colette Kress told investors that the company expects revenue to grow 75% in fiscal 2028, while projecting fourth-quarter revenue of $126 billion to $134 billion, comfortably ahead of the average analyst estimate of just over $125 billion according to LSEG data. Nvidia clarified its forecast did not factor in any data centre chip sales to China. The multiple is also significantly below Nvidia's forward P/E interquartile range of 30-44 times over the past decade, reflecting growing concerns around AI infrastructure financing, leadership uncertainty and the durability of future earnings according to Binance Research.

Asian technology stocks moved higher after the US session, with MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rising 0.9%. South Korea's KOSPI led the gains, climbing as much as 3.3%, while Japan's Nikkei 225 advanced 0.6% and US S&P 500 e-mini futures were up 0.5%. The next major indicator of investor appetite for the AI sector will come from Anthropic, which is preparing to set the price of its shares later on Wednesday ahead of its market debut; the listing could value the company at as much as $1.4 trillion according to Bloomberg News.

Several analysts weighed in on where AI and semiconductors are headed. Michael O'Rourke at JonesTrading said the data centre slowdown due to the political shift is going to be real, that earnings estimates behind valuations no longer valid, and that investors have no idea where those estimates will reset as they de-risk until clarity returns which won't be for some time. Michael Burry sold 25% of his put positions in the $58 billion VanEck Semiconductor ETF amid a deepening rout in US technology stocks, though he noted the SMH put positions even after the sale have become very large positions. Jakub Rochlitz at eToro pointed out that this differs from a regular sell-off because recoveries are not appearing after significant losses such as Intel Corp falling further despite plunging almost 30% on Friday, and there is increasing cross-sector correlation with rising volatility spreading the rout across the market. Chris Zaccarelli at Northlight Asset Management described the all-or-nothing mentality as surprising to them while agreeing sentiment has shifted and building data centres will become more difficult, but argued that if a productive business case exists for building them then they will get built.

The article was written by Veer Sharma, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or Investment Adviser and holds no financial interest in the companies mentioned as of publication; views are those of respective analysts reproduced with attribution. The disclaimer noted that readers should consider original research reports and make investment decisions based on their own assessment.
items.title: Nvidia Earnings Beat Eases AI Fears as IT Stocks Fall and Asian Tech Rises

items.summary: A BBC Watchdog investigation reported that several UK customers who bought high-value electronics from Currys received products that did not match what they ordered. Lucy, identified in the programme, purchased an iPhone for £750 at a Carlisle store but found a dummy handset inside; after two return attempts she received the same fake device each time and eventually recovered her £750 through her bank rather than from Currys directly. Andrew spent £2,700 on an Apple MacBook ordered in black but received a silver model bearing marks left by old stickers; he recorded his replacement being opened at a store only to find the identical machine he had returned about three weeks earlier, and after discovering its warranty had been activated 19 days before his purchase, Currys issued him a full refund plus compensation. Lee paid £3,300 for an Apple MacBook from a Carlisle-area Aldershot store but found two bags of rice instead; when he contacted Apple, the device's 12-month warranty was reported as already activated 16 days before his purchase, Currys declined to reopen his complaint, and he recovered his £750 through his bank with the retailer agreeing to reimburse it. The investigation suggested a possible retail fraud operation in which criminals swap expensive electronics for cheaper substitutes before returning packages; if returned parcels are not properly inspected, contents could re-enter stock and be resold, trapping buyers who pay full price for empty boxes. Currys described incorrect orders as exceptionally rare, said it would investigate such incidents, and noted that outcomes differed between customers: Andrew received a refund and compensation from the retailer, while Lee and Lucy recovered their money through banks after being unable to secure direct refunds.
items.title: Currys customers repeatedly received fake or wrong electronics before recovering payments via their banks

items.summary: Baner police in Pune arrested Hitesh Pramod Kulkarni, a 21-year-old resident of the Inclusive Housing Society near Balewadi High Street, for allegedly defrauding society members of ₹35 lakh. According to police, Kulkarni claimed he had cleared the Union Public Service Commission examination and become an IAS officer; this claim was relayed by his father and subsequently reported in newspapers and on news channels, with The Lions Club also felicitating him. Police said Kulkarni had actually studied only up to Class 12. After moving into the society through an MHADA allotment, he introduced himself as an IAS officer, showed residents the reports to establish credibility, and took steps to get the conveyance deed executed in the society's name from the builder. This helped him gain confidence among residents, many of whom elected him chairman between January 2026 and Nov 15, 2026. Society treasurer Dattatray Vaijnath Nagarjoje, a resident of Rutuja Complex on Sinhagad Road, lodged the complaint that followed. Police said the society collected around ₹37 lakh as one-time maintenance charges from members, which was deposited in a bank. After becoming chairman, Kulkarni allegedly took a ₹10 lakh loan against the society's fixed deposit and used ₹5 lakh for himself; he also allegedly misappropriated ₹27 lakh from the fixed deposit and another ₹3 lakh lying in the society's bank account for personal benefit. Beyond diverting funds, Kulkarni targeted members by claiming several flats were still vacant and had not been sold, promising to allot them through a lottery system while collecting money from interested parties. To make the scheme appear genuine, he allegedly prepared fake allotment letters using ChatGPT and handed them to members. The complainant alleged that society members were collectively cheated of ₹35 lakh. Following the complaint, Baner police registered a case, with Police Sub-Inspector Raju Jadhav investigating.
items.title: Pune Man Arrested for ₹35 Lakh Housing Society Fraud After Posing as IAS Officer and Using ChatGPT to Forge Allotment Letters

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio dismissed concerns about a possible Iranian plot to target Washington, DC with a dirty bomb or chemical weapons, stating the United States does not face an 'imminent threat.' items.summary:
Nvidia beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter earnings and sales, and guided fourth-quarter revenue above the analyst consensus estimate. The company expects Q4 revenue of $126 billion to $134 billion against an average analyst projection of just over $125 billion per LSEG data. Nvidia stated it did not assume any China data center chip sales in its outlook. Interim CEO Colette Kress said, "Our momentum is real," framing the company as a technology leader driven by innovation.

Separately from results, Nvidia's board created a national security and export controls committee earlier Tuesday — its first major governance action since Jensen Huang departed. Washington has tightened licensing rules for chip shipments to Southeast Asia and overseas data centers serving Chinese firms, while lawmakers prepare to question Huang, who had advocated greater exports to China.

Analysts responded with mixed reactions. Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co., New York, called the guide strong and expected a relief rally despite "the black cloud over Nvidia" from the Jensen saga. Nick Giorgi of Alpine Macro, New York, said demand for compute remains insatiable and that market focus has shifted toward who will oversee the company going forward; he viewed the results as positive for AI infrastructure but cautioned investors to weigh governance risk.

Rick Meckler of Cherry Lane Investments, New Vernon, New Jersey, noted the numbers were good but questioned whether they are determinative given an SEC examination reported by The Wall Street Journal and leadership uncertainty. He characterized the day as a sigh of relief rather than a signal for renewed buying, citing legal situations that may make management cautious in statements.

The article includes promotional content from ETMarkets regarding Sensex, Nifty Track, Budget 2025 coverage, Telegram alerts, ET Prime subscriptions, and trending stocks such as SBI, Axis Bank, HDFC Bank, Infosys, Wipro, and NTPC. The source dates reference 2025.
items.title: Nvidia beats earnings and guides to strong fourth-quarter revenue amid leadership uncertainty

items.summary: NVIDIA reported results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2027, showing revenue rising 103% year-on-year to $115.8 billion from $57 billion, with a sequential increase of 20% from $96.2 billion in the prior quarter. The company attributed this growth to accelerating demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure and data centre technology. NVIDIA's Data Center business remained its largest growth engine, generating revenue of $107.6 billion, up 110% year-on-year. Net income climbed 105% to $65.3 billion from $31.9 billion, while operating income rose 115% to $77.5 billion compared with $36 billion a year earlier. Operating expenses increased 57% to $9.2 billion, and gross margin improved to 74.8% from 73.4% the prior year, though it moderated slightly from 75% in the preceding quarter. Diluted earnings per share jumped 108% to $2.70 from $1.30. NVIDIA's investments in other companies reached $109.747 billion as of October 25, 2026, with marketable equity securities accounting for $44.219 billion and non-marketable securities at $65.528 billion. Looking ahead to the fourth quarter of FY27, NVIDIA expects revenue of approximately $130 billion, with a variation of 3%, excluding Data Center compute revenue from China. The company projects GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins between 71% and 72%, operating expenses at about $11 billion under GAAP and $10.7 billion on a non-GAAP basis. These figures reflect continued AI-driven growth, though the outlook notes that margins and rising expenditure remain important factors for investors.
items.title: NVIDIA Reports Q3 FY27 Revenue Jump of 103% to $115.8 Billion on AI Demand

items.summary: On Tuesday (November 17), Jensen Huang issued his first public statement since being unseated from the top job at Nvidia a week earlier. In it, he said he would be willing to return as chief executive if the company's board determined that doing so was in the best interests of shareholders, employees, and the United States. Huang posted the full statement on X, where he thanked supporters for their kindness during the past week, reflecting on his tenure at the AI chipmaker. He wrote: 'I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life.' Huang acknowledged personal failures, stating that 'I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA,' that he had made serious mistakes in his personal life, created problems for the Board that he deeply regrets, owns those mistakes completely, and is committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation. He noted an outpouring of calls from employees, investors, business partners, and customers asking him to return as CEO amid complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics, adding: 'If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.' Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones swiftly rejected the prospect of a return, saying the board does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO. The remarks came as Nvidia reported another blockbuster quarter, with revenue more than doubling from a year earlier and earnings topping Wall Street expectations; notably, the company made no mention of Huang's departure or the possibility of his return in its earnings release. In response to the controversy, Nvidia announced the creation of a board committee to oversee national security and global trade compliance. Meanwhile, key House lawmakers said Huang has agreed to appear for transcribed interviews before congressional committees next month as scrutiny intensifies over Nvidia's advanced chip sales and related national security concerns. The article includes agency inputs; no specific revenue or earnings figures were provided in the source text beyond the description that revenue more than doubled year-over-year and earnings exceeded expectations, so those are not quantified here.
items.title: Huang offers to return as Nvidia CEO; board declines

items.summary: PVR Inox's shares reached a fresh 52-week high of around Rs 1,740 apiece on the NSE, pushing its market capitalisation above Rs 17,060 crore. CRISIL Ratings simultaneously upgraded PVR Inox's outlook to positive and reaffirmed its 'Crisil AA' rating on long-term debt instruments, while also holding short-term bank facilities and commercial paper at 'Crisil A1+'. The ratings agency attributed the outlook upgrade to expectations of sustained growth across multiple revenue streams and improving operating margins that strengthen the business risk profile. It noted the company is projected to become a net cash entity during the first half of fiscal 2027, which CRISIL said further strengthens its financial risk profile. Structural improvement was also credited to PVR Inox's ability to monetise its network more consistently across content cycles, reducing content concentration risk as admissions are supported by a broader mix of Hindi, regional and Hollywood content; the rise of mid-budget films is cited as lowering dependence on marquee releases and stabilising admissions and occupancy. CRISIL acknowledged that these strengths are partially offset by inherent volatility in film exhibition, with operating performance dependent on content quality, timing and evolving consumer preferences.
items.title: CRISIL upgrades PVR Inox outlook as shares hit fresh 52-week high

items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday urged support for free and open trade while opposing protectionism, delivering an opening speech at an Asia-Pacific summit. He called for upholding a rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core, supporting free and open trade and investment, maintaining stable global industrial and supply chains, pursuing closer technology partnerships, and keeping global supply chains stable and open. Xi framed his remarks against what he described as rampant unilateralism and protectionism that are undermining global growth momentum, asserting China's commitment to true multilateralism. His comments came immediately after Washington announced further restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia. The US said the new rules aim to prevent sensitive technology from threatening national security, with officials suspecting restricted Nvidia chips have been diverted to China through overseas companies and data centres. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security stated that the United States is the global leader in advanced computing and super intelligence technology and remains committed to promoting American technology for legitimate commercial purposes while ensuring sensitive technologies are not exploited in ways that threaten US national security. The rules target Chinese companies renting advanced Nvidia computing power through overseas data centres, obtaining processors through Singapore and other countries, with some shipments requiring US export licences. Data-centre operators serving Chinese customers may face stricter customer-verification and licensing requirements, along with possible pressure on utilisation and expansion, while Chinese AI developers could encounter higher costs and slower access to computing power. The announcement follows the revelation of a scandal involving ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a Singapore-based Chinese business executive, after US investigators suspected that Megaspeed was used to illegally divert billions of dollars' worth of restricted Nvidia AI chips into China. In response, China's Ministry of Commerce expressed strong dissatisfaction and firm opposition on Tuesday, urging both countries to resolve differences through consultation and cooperation while warning it would take countermeasures to firmly safeguard its sovereignty, security and development interests if the US persists with curbs on remote access to advanced chips. Xi added that China will continue investing in its industrial complex and developing new technologies that would benefit other countries as well. The restrictions build on major export controls imposed by then-President Joe Biden in 2022 aimed at restricting China's access to advanced AI chips and semiconductor equipment, though US officials believe China has used offshore shell companies like Megaspeed to acquire the restricted chips.
items.title: Xi Calls for Free Trade as China Threatens Retaliation Over US AI Chip Restrictions

items.summary: On Wednesday, security forces killed top Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander Lateef Bhat in an encounter inside a mosque in the Kulgam district of Jammu and Kashmir. The operation was framed by authorities as retaliation for an attack on Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel that occurred seven days earlier. Bhat, described by security forces as the last active local terrorist in the Valley, had been located after an extensive search involving CCTV footage and repeated intelligence inputs; he refused to surrender despite appeals and was neutralised while trapped inside a mosque, with no damage caused to the structure. Union home minister Amit Shah praised the "coordinated efforts" of Jammu and Kashmir Police (JKP), Indian Army, CRPF, and intelligence agencies in neutralising Bhat. He also stated that one associate, Umar Nisar Dar, had been killed the day before. Director General of the CRPF GP Singh posted on X: "Congratulations, guys. Some dishes are best served cold, even in cold weather." The initial attack took place at a CRPF post in Akhran village on November 11, when two armed men opened fire and injured three personnel, one critically; ground verification later established that the attackers approached on foot from a nearby forested area rather than by motorcycle. CCTV footage examined between November 10 and 15 identified Bhat and Dar at multiple locations including Mir Bazar, Akhran, Hablish, and Kilam, documenting their reconnaissance before the attack and their flight afterward. Investigators found that Dar had allegedly provided shelter and logistical assistance to Bhat for five to six months; his family had filed a missing-person report after he disappeared, and officials said Dar joined The Resistance Front (TRF), an offshoot of LeT, after the November 11 attack. On November 16, following intelligence about two suspected terrorists near Laru bypass, security forces conducted another cordon-and-search operation; they evacuated students from two nearby schools before acting, and Dar was killed while Bhat escaped with alleged bullet injuries. On November 17, the search widened across dozens of villages using drones and sniffer dogs, though prolonged restrictions drew criticism from political leaders in Kashmir over hardship to ordinary residents. On November 18, contact with Bhat was re-established during an operation in Zangalpora village in the Devsar area; after he entered a mosque following appeals to surrender via video call involving him, the Kulgam SSP Anayat Ali Chowdhary, and the CEO of the 9 Rashtriya Rifles, police confirmed his death. The report is grounded entirely in statements from security officials and social media posts attributed to Amit Shah and GP Singh; no independent verification of these claims is provided.
items.title: Security forces neutralise LeT commander Lateef Bhat in Kulgam after CRPF post attack

items.summary: According to an India Today report, 37-year-old Akshita Jain has left a lucrative corporate career—backed by an MBA from IIM Bengaluru and roles with Fiat, Mercedes-Benz, and Volkswagen—to embrace Jain asceticism. In her most recent position at Volkswagen, she reportedly earned an annual compensation package of ₹50 lakh. The turning point in her transition came during AI initiatives at work; Akshita grew concerned about the environmental footprint of large data centres, specifically land excavation and harm to microscopic soil organisms. She said this realization aligned with Jain ahimsa (non-violence toward all living beings), prompting renunciation. Her 61-year-old mother, Shiromani Bajaj—retired chief manager at IOCL after a 37-year career ending in October 2025—is joining her. Following her husband's death and household duties, Shiromani reportedly turned to Jain spirituality through close association with sadhvis and completed religious observances and austerities. The Gurugram-based duo is receiving guidance from Sadhvi Purnapragyashree. A traditional varghoda procession was scheduled in Jodhpur, setting up their formal diksha ceremony in Chennai on February 25—a transition formally renouncing worldly attachments to become ascetics. items.title: Corporate professionals renounce careers to become Jain ascetics amid AI-driven environmental concerns

According to reports from The Hindu, senior superintendent of police Anayat Ali Choudhary said security forces had 'a long conversation' with the militant by phone before engaging him. A Border Security Force (BSF) personnel was detained on Tuesday by Bangladesh's border guarding force after he reportedly "inadvertently" crossed the unfenced international border around noon, according to The Indian Express. He returned safely in the evening following a meeting between commanders from both sides.

The security personnel is reported to have crossed the border from Meghalaya's Jowai into Bangladesh's Sylhet district, venturing approximately 200 yards across it, per India Today NE. At the time of his detention, he was reportedly carrying a walkie-talkie, an Indian Small Arms System rifle, and a pump-action gun, according to The Shillong Times.

Videos shared on social media showed two Border Guard Bangladesh personnel along with several residents accompanying the Indian constable after he crossed into Bangladesh. In one video, he is seen being taken away by Bangladeshi personnel on a civilian motorcycle, per The Indian Express. After the Border Security Force took cognisance of these videos, senior officers deployed in Meghalaya contacted their Bangladeshi counterparts and called for a flag meeting, according to The Shillong Times.

The Border Security Force guards a 4,096-km-long stretch of border between India and Bangladesh. All details are drawn from the reporting cited within this item.
items.title: Indian BSF personnel detained after crossing into Bangladesh

items.summary: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar inaugurated the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit, themed 'AI and Beyond', on Tuesday, outlining Karnataka's ambition to expand into artificial intelligence, deep technology, semiconductor manufacturing, and biotechnology. The state earned approximately USD 173 billion in software exports last year, accounting for two out of every five dollars India received through software and services exports; it also drew USD 9.4 billion in FDI equity inflows in the first half of FY 2025-26, representing 26.7 per cent of India's total inflows during that period. More than 1,000 Global Capability Centres have chosen Bengaluru as their base, while over 30 new GCCs brought investments exceeding USD 1 billion into the state in 2025 alone. Karnataka hosts more than 24,000 recognised startups and nearly two out of every five unicorns nationally; Bengaluru ranks among the world's leading startup ecosystems and is second in Asia for AI-native startups. Startups in Bengaluru raised USD 4.4 billion—nearly matching the combined funding of the next five Indian cities—with Karnataka-based ventures raising a cumulative USD 79 billion, and women-led Bengaluru ventures attracting USD 13.4 billion. On talent, Shivakumar said Bengaluru holds nearly half of India's AI and machine learning workforce, with plans for an AI University and an AI Hub; an additional Centre of Excellence at IIIT Raichur would extend AI applications to the 13 districts of North Karnataka across agriculture, healthcare, education, and small businesses. The proposed Bengaluru Robotics and AI Innovation Zone (BRAINZ) is set to further strengthen the ecosystem. Under Nipuna Karnataka, Rs 300 crore has been earmarked for reskilling, with 33,000 people—including women returning after career breaks—made industry-ready. In semiconductors, the state hosts more than 100 fabless companies and three out of every five engineers in India's semiconductor capability centres are based in Bengaluru; Karnataka accounts for one-fifth of India's electronics exports, with companies committing over Rs 23,000 crore to research, development, and manufacturing in Bengaluru and Mysuru. Four electronics manufacturing clusters are being developed between Dharwad and Mysuru under the state's electronics system design and manufacturing policy. The bioeconomy was valued at USD 39.2 billion last year—about one-fifth of India's total and more than 10 per cent of the state's economy—with initiatives underway in marine biotechnology, agriculture, healthcare, genome editing, and gene therapy. On the summit itself, participation rose to more than 75 countries from 57 last year; exhibitors nearly doubled, and business visitor participation is expected to rise by about a third. Startup support continues through ELEVATE, which has provided equity-free grants to 1,500 startups over the past decade; under ELEVATE NxT, 33 deep-tech startups received Rs 30 crore since last year; the proposed Innoverse programme aims to support 35 growth-stage ventures over five years; and Rs 25 crore has been earmarked to procure solutions developed by startups.
items.title: Karnataka Targets Global AI and Semiconductor Hub Amid Software Export Strength

items.summary: India has developed its first indigenous vaccine against the H5N1 avian influenza virus, commonly known as bird flu, to strengthen preparedness for poultry outbreaks. The inactivated vaccine was created by ICAR-NIHSAD (National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases) and targets the H5N1 virus of clade 2.3.2.1a, which has been responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens. Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan is set to dedicate the vaccine at NIHSAD's facility in Bhopal on November 20. According to ICAR-NIHSAD, a single dose provides protection for up to six months and makes the vaccine suitable for layer and breeder chickens; until now, no specific commercial vaccine had been available against this clade of H5N1 virus. The development comes amid fresh bird flu outbreaks in parts of India, including Tamil Nadu's Cuddalore district, where H5N1 infection was confirmed in November following sudden bird deaths at poultry farms and 35,647 birds died as of November 13; authorities initiated culling within a one-kilometre radius, with around 40,000 chickens subsequently reported culled. Andhra Pradesh also reported an outbreak in October in Anantapur district's Siddarampuram village in Bukkarayasamudram mandal, prompting the state government to declare infected and surveillance zones and restrict poultry movement. Bird flu, or highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), can cause severe disease and high mortality among poultry; since it was first detected in India in 2006, more than 500 combined outbreaks of H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes have been reported. The government says the H5N1 clade 2.3.2.1a strain has also been detected in different animal species, including mammals, as well as in three human cases; separately, the World Health Organization has reported 1,003 human cases of H5N1, including 479 deaths, across 25 countries since 2003. The indigenous vaccine is expected to add another tool to India's efforts to control outbreaks, alongside surveillance, testing, biosecurity and culling.
items.title: India develops its own H5N1 vaccine amid fresh bird flu outbreaks

items.summary: State Food Safety officials seized 1,240 kg of edible oil from Bolas Agro Private Limited on November 17 at the Baikampady Industrial Area in Dakshina Kannada district. The seizure followed alleged misbranding and labelling violations: raw groundnut oil was procured from Challakere in Chitradurga district, then repackaged and sold as cold pressed groundnut oil. The seized stock comprised 11 boxes of groundnut oil (10 kg per box), 30 cans of groundnut oil (35 litres per can), and 4 boxes of coconut oil (20 kg per box). Officials stated the operation was conducted by the Food Safety and Drug Administration Department.
items.title: Karnataka Seizes 1,240 kg of Edible Oil Over Misbranding in Dakshina Kannada

During a search of the vehicle, officers recovered gold jewellery that had been looted from it.
